recent_posts.title: Visual Studio Code 1.120
recent_posts.summary: VS Code 1.120 (Insiders) release notes covering updates from May 4–7, 2026. Key changes include grouping chat sessions by recency, a context size picker in the model picker, hiding archived chat sessions by default, surfacing GitHub pull request metadata in agent host UI, secure handling of password prompts in chat agent terminal commands (secrets never routed through the model), Copilot CLI plugin discovery, agent terminals respecting user shell preferences, a new customDiffEditorProvider proposed API for extensions, restored ability to copy code from chat edit removal suggestions, a custom snooze duration for inline suggestions, and reduced CSS context when attaching DOM elements to chat.

recent_posts.title: VS Code Release Highlights - April 2026
recent_posts.summary: VS Code April 2026 release highlights include the new Agents Window (now in preview as a companion app for agent-first development workflows), a chat customizations evaluations extension for analyzing and optimizing prompt files and custom agents, configurable thinking effort in Copilot CLI, remote control for Copilot CLI sessions via github.com or GitHub mobile, and a new Learn section on the VS Code docs site with introductory courses on agent foundations and customization.

recent_posts.title: Visual Studio Code 1.119
recent_posts.summary: VS Code 1.119 (Insiders) release notes covering updates from April 29–30, 2026. Key additions include a Markdown preview button, the ability to hide the update notification button in the title bar, reorganized Markdown settings, support for indexing external ingest in virtual file systems for chat codebase context, attaching browser tabs to chat for page snapshot context, Copilot CLI plan mode in AHP, and agent permission dialogs for browser tab access.

recent_posts.title: Let's Build a Custom Agent! | Ep 4 of 8
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of building custom agents in GitHub Copilot within VS Code. Covers what custom agents are, how to configure them with specific personas, tools, and instructions, and demonstrates creating a security reviewer agent and an arcade-themed app builder agent. Shows how to use Copilot itself to suggest and generate custom agent configurations, then applies the agent to build a new tip calculator app that inherits the styling and architecture of an existing project.

recent_posts.title: How to use GitHub Copilot agent skills in your workflow
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot agent skills are folders of instructions, scripts, and resources that Copilot can load to perform specialized tasks. They work as an open standard across GitHub Copilot in VS Code, Copilot CLI, and Copilot Cloud Agent. A practical walkthrough demonstrates creating a custom skill that automatically updates a README file whenever a new feature is added to a project, including how to modify the skill to send a chat confirmation after updating.

recent_posts.title: GitHub Copilot customization features explained with comparison charts and quizzes
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of GitHub Copilot's customization features in VS Code, specifically comparing custom instructions, prompt files, custom agents, agent skills, and hooks. Uses Copilot itself to explain the differences through summaries, comparison charts, and interactive quizzes, then consolidates everything into a reusable HTML reference file.

recent_posts.title: How to use GitHub Copilot custom instructions in VS Code
recent_posts.summary: GitHub Copilot custom instructions in VS Code act as a persistent rulebook for the AI, letting developers define coding styles, conventions, and standards that Copilot automatically applies in every chat session. The tutorial demonstrates creating a SOLID principles instruction file for code refactoring and generating a WCAG accessibility instruction file using Copilot itself via the /create instructions command. Custom instructions are especially powerful for teams, ensuring consistent naming, formatting, and architectural patterns across a shared repository without manual review overhead.

recent_posts.title: Hooks: The Underestimated Feature | Ep 5 of 8
recent_posts.summary: VS Code Copilot hooks let you execute custom shell commands at lifecycle points during agent sessions. This tutorial demonstrates creating a user-level Copilot hook that automatically runs Prettier after every file edit using the post-tool-use lifecycle event, showing how to generate the hook via Copilot agent customizations and verify it works in a real project.

recent_posts.title: How to use prompt files in VS Code with GitHub Copilot
recent_posts.summary: Prompt files are reusable markdown files that store instructions for AI chat sessions in VS Code with GitHub Copilot. Instead of retyping complex prompts repeatedly, you define them once and invoke them with a slash command. The video demonstrates creating a prompt file to quiz you on open code files and another to simplify bloated code, showing how to scope them at workspace or user level for reuse across projects.

top_posts.title: Visualize data structures and algorithms
top_posts.summary: Visualize data structures directly in VS Code using the Debug Visualizer extension. This tool allows you to run the Debug Visualizer New View command, evaluate expressions, and choose visualization methods. You can interact with visuals and observe changes in real-time, making it especially useful for learning data structures or understanding algorithms during debugging sessions.

top_posts.title: Simplify debugging with log points in VS Code
top_posts.summary: Reduce clutter from multiple console.log statements in your code by using log points in Visual Studio Code. Right-click on the gutter of the desired line, select 'Add Logpoint', and write your message. This method provides on-demand logging and eliminates the need for cleanup before deployment.

top_posts.title: Python is the most downloaded VS Code extension with 200 million downloads
top_posts.summary: The Python extension is the most downloaded VS Code extension ever with 200 million downloads, far surpassing GitHub Copilot (68 million) and Maven for Java (42.8 million). The extension provides IntelliSense, debugging, formatting, linting, and other Python development features.

top_posts.title: Enhance productivity with AI + Remote Dev
top_posts.summary: VS Code enhances developer productivity by integrating AI with its remote development capabilities. The integration allows for seamless AI-driven coding whether on local or remote setups. Key features include custom instructions that tailor AI responses to specific coding practices, chat participants to assist with remote environment setup, and agent mode for autonomous coding sessions. These innovations help streamline workflows in various development environments, including SSH, containers, and GitHub Codespaces.

top_posts.title: Visualizer Data Structures in VS Code
top_posts.summary: The debug visualizer extension in VS Code allows you to visualize data structures directly during debugging. Users can specify an expression to evaluate and choose how to visualize it, such as viewing linked lists as graphs or arrays as grids. This interactive tool can be particularly helpful for learning data structures or understanding algorithm behavior.
